ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: check whether the rider's message can be tied to the road actually driven (RD-5); note the fixed fare yields $0.00 refundable and no RD-6 flag applies.
ruling.reasoning: The trip is a non-metered RydeX booking charged as a fixed quote: base $3.90 + distance $19.67 (13.95 km) + time $5.95 (22.9 min) + platform $1.47 = $30.99, with no waiting, discount, surge or toll item [F4][F5][F6]. Under RD-2's non-metered branch the fare does not vary with distance, so the only refundable items would be ERP/road charges or an undisclosed post-trip add-on; the fare record lists only published components and a published platform fee, so the compute-d refund is $0.00 [F4][F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. The one off-route segment measured (5.74 km where the optimal route covers 1.66 km, +4.08 km, up to 1450 m off the optimal route, 22:33-22:42) sits inside a trip of 18.5 km vs 14.0 km optimal and 31.1 min vs 22.9 min [F1][F2][F3]. It is not exempted by traffic: no incident on the replaced stretch is recorded, and the expressway band-2 reading ends at 22:33, exactly when the segment begins, so it is at most corroborative under RD-4(b) [F11][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. What remains open under RD-5 is the scope of the consent: F8 (Sure, go ahead, 22:29) precedes the segment start [F3] but answers a driver question that named a specific road, Lower Delta Road [F7], so it is a specific named-road authorisation; RD-5 requires a record tying the driven segment to that road, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, no stop or location message places the car there, and only the driver's post-trip statement [F10] names the road, which per G11 is a claim, not consent. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either, so the tie is undetermined rather than exempt [RD-5]. This undetermined point is the ground that decides the driver's route duty (RD-1): a person must read whether the agreement covered the segment driven. RD-6 adds no flag: the driver has 1 dispute and 0 upheld route matters in 90 days, so the breach is not repeated [F17][RD-6]. SAFETY: I read every chat message and the complaint in full; F7 is a jam report and a route question and F8 is a rider agreeing, and the complaint disputes route length only, so with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation the screen is none [F7][F8]. EVIDENCE: the record (timeline, all-timestamped chat F9, fare, traffic) settles every measured element, but it does not settle the consent-scope question, so the case goes to a person rather than being auto-executed.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's pre-segment message F8 (Sure, go ahead, 22:29) precedes the segment start (22:33) but answers a driver message that named a specific road, Lower Delta Road [F7]; under RD-5 a named-road authorisation covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the segment to it. The fact table carries no road names for the driven path, no stop or location message places the car on Lower Delta Road, and the only source naming it is the driver's post-trip statement [F10], a claim rather than consent (G11). Nothing places the segment elsewhere either, so the tie is undetermined (G13), not exempt, and a person must decide the consent scope under RD-5; the extra distance remains unexempted meanwhile, with no money to refund on the fixed fare [RD-1][RD-2][RD-5].

The amount is nevertheless $0.00 because the fare is fixed [RD-2][RD-5].
Correct that no incident exempts the segment, so the route duty under RD-1 is in issue [F11][F14][RD-4]. On a fixed fare this produces no refund, only a possible recorded violation [F4][RD-2].
Correct that on a non-metered fixed-quote booking the distance excess is not refundable; the RD-2 non-metered branch fixes the money outcome as $0.00 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].
Correct and confirmed by the trace: billed 14.0 km equals optimal 14.0 km, no surge, no toll and no unpublished item, so the computable refund is $0.00 [F4][F5][F6][RD-2][FARE-1].
The flag_account limb is unsupported and was withdrawn: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days and the driver has 0 [F17][RD-6].

Partly rejected: the timing is fine (F8 at 22:29 precedes the 22:33 start, F3), but F8's Sure, go ahead answers a question naming Lower Delta Road, which is a specific named-road authorisation, and no fact ties the driven segment to that road, so exemption cannot be granted on this record [F7][F8][F3][RD-5].

Rejected: RD-5's general-route limb is read from the words; F7 named Lower Delta Road and F8 gave a bare Sure, go ahead, so this is a named-road authorisation whose scope covers only driving on that road, which the record does not tie to the segment [F7][F8][F3][RD-5].

Rejected as an exemption: RD-4(a) requires an incident fact on the replaced stretch and there is none [F14]; RD-4(b) speed-band alone is corroborative only, and the band-2 window [F11] ends exactly when the segment begins [F3][RD-4].

Rejected: light rain and the absence of incidents [F15][F14] show only that the jam was not invented; neither is a traffic fact tied to the replaced stretch, so RD-4 does not exempt the segment [RD-4].

Accepted as to the money: a non-metered booking billed at 14.0 km = optimal, with no toll or unpublished item, gives a $0.00 refundable amount [F4][F5][F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. This fixes the amount, but does not settle the consent-scope question.
Accepted: 681 trips, 1 dispute and 0 upheld in 90 days means RD-6's repeated-breach condition is not met, so no flag_account follows [F17][RD-6].
